what: Method names and f-string specs in the card headings are set in Bangers, an all-capitals font, so a chapter about letter case shows UPPER(), LOWER(), TITLE(), CAPITALIZE(), STRIP(), ISDIGIT(), STARTSWITH(X), .FORMAT(), {SCORE=} and '!R AND !S'. Python is case-sensitive: `!R` is a SyntaxError and `name.UPPER()` an AttributeError, so the headings teach code that doesn't run.
evidence:
Measured in the browser (probe.js): 18 headings whose computed font is Bangers and whose text is code: P13 upper()/lower()/title()/capitalize(); P15 strip()/lstrip()/rstrip()/strip(".!"); P24 count(x)/startswith(x)/endswith(x); P25 isdigit()/isalpha()/isspace()/isupper(); P38 {score=} and '!r and !s'; P40 .format(). Markup: `
  • upper()EVERY LETTER BIG.
    • ` with `.toolbox li b { font: 400 1.05rem/1.1 var(--f-title) }` (py-ch11.css:18). Crops: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-py-11-15/a11/w1280-022-p13.png, a11/w390-060-p38.png.
fix: Wrap each name in code, `upper()`: the engine already resets code inside headings to the mono font with `text-transform: none` (comic.css:358). Before: `.toolbox li b { font: … var(--f-title) }` with bare `upper()` → After: `upper()` (why: code must show the case the reader has to type).

what: The hanging-indent wrapper puts break points at every space, including spaces inside string literals, so a wrapped line can end in `"` and start the next with `"`: `replace("` / `", "-")`, `raw.split(",` / `")`. A space that is the whole point of the string becomes invisible.

fix: In hangLines, don't insert `<wbr>`/break opportunities inside highlighted `.s` (string) spans shorter than ~12 characters; wrap the whole string token with `white-space: nowrap` instead.
